title: Divergence: lower_spec_fn_body result-narrowing gate (block_result_is_int_literal_arith) misses literal-free spec arithmetic — `spec fn double(n: u64) -> u64 dec n { n + n }` is E0308 -> L0; Verus types ALL spec arithmetic as int, not only literal-mentioning arithmetic

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Failing tests at forge/tests/divergence_noliteral_spec_arith.rs::literal_free_arith_spec_fn_certifies_l3 and ::literal_free_two_param_arith_spec_fn_certifies_l3 demonstrate the divergence (run with --ignored; both assert design-§6 L3, both observe L0 with E0308 'expected u64, found int' on the bare 'n + n' / 'a + b' result). Root cause: block_result_is_int_literal_arith requires expr_mentions_int_literal, but Verus types ALL spec arithmetic as int — the literal mention is incidental to the #237 repro, not the typing trigger. Fail-closed (no false certification). Also adjudicated this re-audit: the #237 narrowing is NOT a soundness change — live probe shows an out-of-range narrowed value is OPAQUE to verus (postcondition 'result == big(0)' with big = (u64::MAX + 1) as u64 and body 0 FAILS, i.e. no silent-wrap certification; truncating semantics would have certified it).

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Critic plan: pin the gap as two #[ignore]d live-verus failing tests in forge/tests/divergence_noliteral_spec_arith.rs (design-§6 L3 expected vs observed L0/E0308), commit them as the audit artifact per the #233-chain convention. No production code touched — the fix is the generator's.
